summary: This program prints a numbered pizza menu, reads the customer's choice from the keyboard, and either confirms the order or reports an invalid selection. It brings together an array, a for loop, a ternary operator, and an if/else statement.

lines.text: The three menu items live in a single array rather than three separate variables, so the menu can be displayed with one loop and checked against one length.
Array positions start at 0, but a customer expects the menu to start at 1, so the loop prints i + 1 as the label while still reading pizzas[i].
The ternary operator asks hasNextInt() whether the waiting input really is a whole number before calling nextInt(). If someone types letters, choice becomes -1 instead of the program crashing.
Both halves of the range must hold, which is why && joins them. Comparing against pizzas.length rather than the literal 3 means the check still works if you add a fourth pizza to the array.
Subtracting 1 converts the customer's menu number back into an array index, undoing the i + 1 used when the menu was printed.
Closing the Scanner releases the input it was holding, a habit worth forming now even though this short program is about to end anyway.
